To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we propose a new dual path network (DPN) which combines the benefits of ResNet (feature re usage) and DenseNet (feature exploration) for better image classification; (2) we show that ResNet and DenseNet are equivalent in the HORNN framework; and (3) we demonstrate that DPN achieves state-of-the-art performance in image classification on ImageNet, Places365, and PASCASL VOC datasets.

(1) the state of the arts, ResNet and DenseNet, can be interpreted as two different connection path topologies in HORNN, (2) ResNet and DenseNets can be combined to form a new Dual Path Network (Dense Residual Network), and (3) DPNs are simple, highly efficient, and can be trained in a fully convolutional manner with a very small memory consumption, which leads to better performance on a variety of tasks
(1) the ResNet and DenseNet are both special cases of the HORNN, and (2) a dual path network can combine the best of both worlds, achieving state of the art results.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental question of how to learn good representations for visual recognition.
the fundamental problem of how to design efficient network architecture for image classification, and the proposed DPN is a simple yet highly effective solution to this problem.
the design of new network architectures for image classification.

DPN is the best single model for image classification, detection and segmentation tasks.
our proposed DPN achieves state of the art performance on image classification with much less computational cost.
DPNs can achieve better performance and faster training speed than the state of the arts with much less computational cost and model size.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DPN is the most efficient network among the state of the arts for image classification.
we present a new architecture for deep neural networks which can be easily extended for various applications.
we propose a novel network structure that can be used as a drop-in replacement for ResNet and DenseNet, which achieves state of the art performance on various datasets and applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
dual path networks provide a new way to explore the tradeoff between feature reuse and feature exploration for better performance.
the dual path architecture is a simple, yet effective way to design a powerful image classification network.
a simple yet powerful DPN model is capable of achieving state-of-the-art performance with a much smaller model size, lower computational cost and lower memory consumption.
